key_insight: Powder-in-tube mechanical confinement turns brittle Heusler caloric powders into fatigue-resistant composites by preventing catastrophic fragmentation and improving load transfer.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable design strategy for durable solid-state cooling materials that can survive the repeated loading required for practical caloric refrigeration.
method: Packed Heusler alloy powder to 87% density inside a ductile steel tube (2.8 mm OD, 0.3 mm wall).
Applied cyclic mechanical loading while measuring strain and AC magnetic susceptibility simultaneously in situ.
Used the combined signals to probe heterogeneous internal stress and transformation behavior under load.
evidence_signal: The composites survived 100,000 load cycles at 250 MPa without structural failure and withstood overloads up to 700 MPa.
watch_item: Macroscopic strain alone does not track the martensitic phase fraction in these heterogeneous composites, so interpretation requires coupled mechanical and magnetic measurements.
paper_title: Powder-in-tube confinement as a design principle for fatigue-resistant caloric materials
